threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still navigate by landmarks instead of bus stops. Everyone knows 'the big Tesco' isn’t a valid direction.
Caught the N68 last night; a guy was passionately detailing his conspiracy theory about the old market being haunted. Quite the ride!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy playing accordion on the U7, while a couple argued over who ran the best döner shop in the area.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Ever notice the street art on the U-Bahn trains? It’s like a moving gallery that changes daily. You won’t find that in any other city.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they ignore the BART delays; they’ve got a backup plan for getting across town that doesn’t involve waiting in line.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in the Tenderloin get off the 47, pop a wheely on his bike, then hug a streetlight like it was his long-lost friend. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all cats are stray here, but the neighbourhood's full of proud owners who let their pets roam freely. It's not a cat commune!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still baffled by the 'dibus' signs in the metro, squinting at the map while everyone else walks past like pros.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You start referring to the bus stops by their old names instead of the new ones. Locals will spot that misstep right away.
Last night on the 37, a lady brought her pet ferret on board. It was just chilling in her backpack, poking its head out. Classic Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy selling fresh baklava by the U-Bahn while a busker played Turkish folk tunes. That mix is Neukölln in a nutshell.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg does your late-night döner come with a side of karaoke from the kebab shop next door. It's wild and somehow comforting.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they curse at BART delays while still finishing their burrito from La Taqueria.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 in rush hour, packed like sardines. An accordion player jumped on and played ‘La Vie en Rose’. It was surreal amid the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars in Gràcia are trendy, but some of the best ones are hidden in back alleys, where old locals still sit playing cards.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still take photos of every menu and can't resist asking for a 'mojito de fresa' at a traditional tapas bar.
